# How to Use AI to Write a Polite Repair Request to Your Landlord

> **In short:** You can use any AI assistant to turn your notes about a broken appliance or leak into a short, polite, dated repair request. The most important thing: send it in writing (email or a tenant portal), and keep a copy, because a written record is what protects you later.

Asking a landlord for a repair can feel awkward, especially when you're worried about seeming like a bother. The good news is that a clear, friendly written request is easier to write than most people expect. In this guide you'll describe the problem in plain facts, ask an AI assistant to draft a calm message, and send it in a way that leaves a paper trail. This is for anyone who rents, whether you live in an apartment, a house or a shared home.

## Before you start
- **An AI assistant account.** Any AI chat tool works, and a free account is usually enough for a short letter like this.
- **Your lease and your landlord's contact method.** Find out whether repairs go through email, a tenant portal or a form. Your lease is also where you'll see the name you rent under.
- **Your phone or a notes app, and a few photos.** Photos help, and they're easy to take.
- **About 20 to 30 minutes.** Most of that is writing down the facts.

This guide doesn't replace legal advice. What your landlord must fix, and how quickly, depends on your lease and your local rules. If the problem is serious, a local tenant organization or a legal aid office can tell you what applies to you.

## Step 1 — Write down the facts before you open the AI
Before you type anything into an AI tool, write the facts on paper or in a notes app. Note what is broken, where it is, when you first noticed it, what you've already done about it (did you tell anyone, or take a photo?), and whether it's getting worse. Keep each fact short and specific. "The kitchen faucet drips about once a second, day and night" is far more useful than "the sink is bad." AI can only work with what you give it, so good facts make a good letter. A short list of five to eight facts is plenty. You're not writing the letter yet, just gathering the material.

💬 Example: write a line like "Bathroom sink, drips steadily since March 3, slow leak onto the cabinet floor, photo taken March 4."

You'll know it worked when you have a short, dated list that a stranger could understand without asking you a single question.

## Step 2 — Open a new chat and describe the problem plainly
Open a new chat with your AI assistant. You should see an empty conversation with a message box at the bottom of the screen. Look for a place to type, which is usually at the bottom. Tap or click it, then type a clear request that includes your facts. Plain wording works best. Don't worry about sounding formal; the AI will do the polishing. Send the message, and the assistant's answer will appear below yours. Usually it will ask follow-up questions or offer a draft. If the answer seems to ignore your facts, don't argue with it. Just add a sentence that corrects it and send again.

💬 Example: "My landlord needs to know about a repair. Here are my facts: [paste your facts here]. My name is [your name] and my unit is [unit number]."

You'll know it worked when the assistant's reply mentions your specific problem and dates, not just general advice about landlords.

## Step 3 — Ask for a calm, dated request
Now ask for the actual letter, and tell the AI exactly what tone and content you want. A calm message with a clear request, a date and a reasonable time frame is the goal. You can also ask for a short subject line, which makes the message easy to find later. Because you're asking for a draft, you'll probably get a letter with blanks or placeholders. That's normal. Read the draft through once, and if anything sounds too emotional or blaming, ask for a softer version. Be ready to ask again. Most first drafts need one or two rounds of small changes.

💬 Example: "Please draft a short, polite repair request email to my landlord. Use a calm, friendly tone. Include the facts I listed, today's date as [today's date], and ask for the repair within [number] days. End by asking them to confirm in writing."

You'll know it worked when you have a letter of about one short screen with a subject line, a clear request and a polite closing.

## Step 4 — Check the draft against your facts
AI drafts sometimes add details you didn't give, or get a date wrong. Before you send anything, check every fact against your notes. Make sure the dates, room, appliance and any amounts are right. Delete any sentence that says something you can't back up, such as "this has been happening for months" if you only noticed it last week. Also remove any blame or insults. A factual letter is more likely to get a quick response, and it reads well later if you ever need to show what you reported and when.

💬 Example: "Please remove any statement I can't confirm from my facts, and keep the letter under [number] sentences."

You'll know it worked when every sentence in the letter matches a fact you wrote down in Step 1.

## Step 5 — Send it in writing and save a copy
Send the letter through the method your lease or landlord uses. Email is common, and a tenant portal or a written form also works. Paste the final text into your email or form, add your name and unit, and send it. Then save a copy: keep the sent email in a folder, or take a screenshot of the portal confirmation. Write down the date you sent it. If you call the landlord about the same problem, follow up with a short written note afterward so the call is also on paper. A phone call alone leaves no record.

💬 Example: a subject line like "Repair request for [unit number]: bathroom sink leak, reported [today's date]."

You'll know it worked when you have a sent message or confirmation with today's date, and a saved copy in a folder you can find again.

## Step 6 — Keep a simple repair log
A short log turns one letter into a record. Make a note in your phone with the date you reported the problem, the date you sent the request, any reply you get and any new details, such as the problem getting worse. Add photos with dates. If nothing happens by the time frame you asked for, you'll have everything in one place. The AI can help here too. Paste your log and ask for a summary if you need to review the timeline.

💬 Example: "Please turn these dated notes into a short timeline I can reread: [paste your log here]."

You'll know it worked when you can read your entire repair history in under a minute.

## Step 7 — Write a polite follow-up if you don't hear back
If you don't get a reply within the time you asked for, send a short follow-up. Keep it friendly and refer to your first message by its date. A follow-up that restates the facts and asks for a reply is usually enough. If the problem is an emergency, such as a gas smell or flooding, contact emergency services or your utility company first, not an AI tool. The AI can draft the message, but it cannot send it for you, check the repair or know the rules that apply to your lease.

💬 Example: "Please draft a short, polite follow-up to my repair request sent on [date of first request]. Restate the problem in one sentence and ask for a reply by [date]."

You'll know it worked when your follow-up refers to the earlier message by date and asks for a specific next step.

## Common mistakes
- **Sending the letter only by text or phone.** The fix is to send it in writing, through email or the portal your lease names, and keep a copy.
- **Letting the AI invent details.** Drafts can add facts you never gave them. The fix is Step 4: check every date, room and number against your notes before you send.
- **Writing in anger.** An angry message can feel good but is easier to dismiss. The fix is to ask the AI for a calm version, and to stick to facts.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** Use the same method for any issue at home, such as a noisy neighbor, a broken lock or a late package delivery. Facts, a date and a polite request work almost everywhere.
- **For your business or work:** The same approach helps with any written request to a vendor, property manager or service provider, because a clear, dated record is easy for everyone to follow.
- **If you're just getting started:** Begin with a small problem, like a dripping faucet. Practice Steps 1 to 5 once, and you'll find the next request much easier.

## Try it now
Pick one small problem in your home right now, such as a drawer that won't close. Write three facts about it in your notes app, then type them into an AI assistant with this request: "Please draft a short, polite repair request to my landlord about [the problem]." Read the draft once, and you'll have a working letter in about two minutes.
